body: If you want it merged, you need to set it ready to review, and we have a flock of agents rip your assumptions apart before merging. :)

<!-- pr-reviewer: b6bc94239655225bdda3e6a83d49d2e996f1018a -->
The code is good. One item is requested before merge: screenshots.

What I checked in the code:

- `controller.post` reads through `parse_post_name` (shape only: a non-empty string, trimmed); a bad value is refused at the key's name. The registry rule (a built-in name that serves the kind) is `post_name_refusal`, and the registry reaches the post crate through a closure, as the holder lookup does (#828). No new crate edge; the decision record is in `docs/decisions/2374-machine-names-its-post.md`.
- `post_offer_for`: the machine's named post wins over the kind offer; it is offered only when it is in the registry, serves the mount, and differs from the setup's post. `PostRef::Builtin` and a named `Fanuc` compare by name, so the default document is never offered its own post. A `File` post is never second-guessed, as before.
- The Setup banner shows the reason ("the machine names X as its post; switch to it?" / the old kind wording); the Machines editor draws a dropdown with `(none)` for "not stated", and `post_choices` lists only the posts that serve the machine's kind. The `Switch post` button takes the existing `SelectPostNamed` command, so undo works as the law asks.
- MCP: `get_job` and `load_machine` answer through one `offer_view`, so a person and an agent are told the same thing. The `post` tool now lists every built-in post. The shipped grblHAL, TinyG, Haas, Tormach, Makera, Sienci and Doosan mill files name their post, and `machine_library` checks each shipped file.
- Provenance: one line, names the public sources. Clean-room: original key and rule, from the issue.

Local results (built and tested on this head, LinuxCNC worktree):

- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: 12 binaries, all passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test machine_library --test mcp_machine_post --test plasma_post`: 14 + 4 + 5 passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`: 1046 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Requested before merge:

1. PR body, `Screenshots`: add viewable before and after images. This PR changes what a user sees: the Machines editor's post field becomes a dropdown, and the Setup banner gets the new "the machine names ..." line. The project asks each UI PR for both images in the body. Post them as release assets or upload them into the PR, and link them from the body.

No other blockers. The PR is ready; I leave it as its author set it. A maintainer approves and merges by hand.
